newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to sell wheat locally, still needs imports.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to sell wheat locally, still needs imports.

text.p: The Turkish Grain Board (TMO), the state agency that buys grain from farmers, will step into the market by selling wheat to local millers to curb rising bread prices, but it still needs to import an unspecified amount of wheat soon, Agriculture Minister Musa Demirci said on Tuesday.

"We will issue a decree that will enable the TMO to sell in the local market at prices it purchased," he told a news briefing. "But we will import wheat for precautionary reasons to support TMO stocks," he said.
Demirci said the decree would change a ruling that requires the TMO to sell at least 15 higher than its purchase prices.

Local wheat and bread prices have risen about 30 percent in the past three weeks after news three weeks ago that Turkey was cracking down on imports from the United States, its main supplier of cereals, due to inspections against ergot fungus.

The government later backed down after pressure from millers, traders and U.S. officials, easing the zero-tolerance level for ergot fungus to first 0.02 percent and later to an unofficial 0.05 percent.
Farm officials said a government decree that would raise the level to 0.05 percent would come out soon.
Demirci said Turkey had imported about 1.5 million tonnes of wheat until the beginning of November out of import licences granted to millers totalling 3.2 million tonnes.
"With our measures of TMO sales and imports, the bread prices will fall to about 15,000 lira (per loaf) from 18,000 lira," he said.

Millers said the TMO should sell at least 100,000 tonnes from its total milling wheat stocks of about 700,000 tonnes to cause a drop to 22,000 lira per kg of wheat in the local market from the current levels of up to 26,000 lira.
Demirci said last week the TMO could import up to 500,000 tonnes of wheat through a tender.
A grain official told Reuters the tender would be held "as soon as possible for an unspecified amount." --Ercan Ersoy, Ankara Newsroom, 90-312-4462940
